documents.unit: Office of the VP for Academic Affairs, Academic Integrity
documents.title: FAQ: AI (Faculty)
documents.stance_why: The FAQ mostly handles reporting, but its one AI answer says "If the use of artificial intelligence is not authorized for the assignment in question, the violation is 'cheating'", so AI is barred unless authorized, which is restrict (not delegates, as no tiers or templates are offered).
documents.summary: Faculty FAQ from the UNT Academic Integrity Office. It treats unauthorized AI as cheating under Policy 6.003 and explains how instructors report, meet with the student, and handle appeals.

units.why: Defines AI use as cheating when unauthorized: "any form of 'unauthorized assistance' constitutes cheating". It tells instructors how to classify AI misuse, so it is P36 (misconduct classification) rather than a penalty rule; addressed to instructors during misuse handling.
units.anchor: any form of "unauthorized assistance" constitutes cheating

units.why: Sets the fallback: "If the use of artificial intelligence is not authorized for the assignment in question, the violation is 'cheating'". AI is effectively banned unless authorized, which is the silent-or-unauthorized fallback of P06.
units.anchor: If the use of artificial intelligence is not authorized for the assignment in question, the
units.fit_note: Stated as how to label a violation, not directly as a student rule.

units.why: The threshold "a preponderance of evidence shows the student violated the policy" is a standard of proof for filing a report, hence P69.
units.anchor: A report should be filed if an instructor decides that a preponderance of evidence shows

units.why: Procedural rule: "Use the Academic Violation Report - Single Violation form for EACH violation." Required form and filing steps are P81.
units.anchor: Use the Academic Violation Report - Single Violation form for EACH violation

units.why: "cases must be reported to the Academic Integrity Office for each violation" is a duty to report to a central office, P81.
units.anchor: cases must be reported to the Academic Integrity Office for each violation

units.why: Rule on combining reports: "You may now file one form for multiple violations so long as the violations were all part of a single incident on a single date." Procedure for reporting, P81.
units.anchor: You may now file one form for multiple violations so long as the violations were

units.why: Requires a conversation first: "you need to meet with the student ... to give the student the opportunity to tell their side of the story." That is P57 (talk before escalating).
units.anchor: you need to meet with the student in person, or on a video platform like

units.why: Covers the case where the student does not respond: "If the student does not respond ... within 5 business days or declines the meeting, you may file the form". It is a procedure on the meeting step; nearest type is P57.
units.anchor: If the student does not respond to you within 5 business days or declines the
units.fit_note: Adds a fallback after 5 business days of no response, which P57 does not cover.

units.why: Gives a timing rule: "Our guidance is to file as soon as you identify the violation." Reporting procedure, P81.
units.anchor: Our guidance is to file as soon as you identify the violation

units.why: States confidentiality: "the AI Office is not at liberty to disclose that information" to instructors about outcomes or prior violations. A procedural limit after reporting; nearest is P81.
units.anchor: the AI Office is not at liberty to disclose that information
units.fit_note: About what the integrity office may not tell instructors (FERPA), not about what instructors must do.

units.why: "The student has the due process right to appeal each violation separately" gives accused students a right to contest; P64.
units.anchor: The student has the due process right to appeal each violation separately

units.why: Appeal routing and advice: appeals go "to the chair of the department" and instructors "should avoid discussing the violation with your chair" until appeal is known. Process steps for integrity cases, P81.
units.anchor: you should avoid discussing the violation with your chair until you determine whether the student

units.why: Mentions a Canvas module "including instruction and a quiz on the UNT Academic Integrity Policy" and a full course; this offers integrity training materials for students, P70.
units.anchor: This module , including instruction and a quiz on the UNT Academic Integrity Policy, may
units.fit_note: Integrity training, not specifically AI literacy.

units.why: Gives the rationale: "academic integrity a value intrinsic to education and to the validity of a UNT degree" - integrity and honest evaluation, P95.
units.anchor: academic integrity a value intrinsic to education and to the validity of a UNT degree

units.why: Says "faculty, administration, and students all have had input on the formulation of Student Academic Integrity Policy"; describes how the policy was made, P84.
units.anchor: The faculty, administration, and students all have had input on the formulation
units.fit_note: Concerns the general integrity policy, not an AI-specific one.

units.why: Directs instructors to "the Academic Integrity Decision Tree" that "will walk you through the academic integrity process"; a pointer to further guidance, P115.
units.anchor: Check out the Academic Integrity Decision Tree

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence guide: Faculty
documents.stance_why: The page says "All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI" and then offers sample statements for allowing with attribution or prohibiting, so the decision is left to instructors with templates.
tiers: Allow AI with attribution (including encourage with three principles)
documents.summary: Library guide for faculty that asks every syllabus to state AI rules, warns that a detector report alone is not enough evidence, and gives sample syllabus statements from prohibiting to encouraging AI.

units.why: "All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI" requires an AI statement in every syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI

units.why: Says detection tools are inadequate ("the inadequacy of detection tools"), so detectors cannot be relied upon: P39.
units.anchor: the inadequacy of detection tools

units.why: Evidence standard: "a detection report alone (such as Turnitin) is not sufficient evidence for a violation". It sets what evidence suffices, so P69 rather than P39, which is about not relying on detectors in general.
units.anchor: a detection report alone (such as Turnitin) is not sufficient evidence for a violation

units.why: The guide supplies "examples for teachers" to use in designing courses, i.e. sample syllabus language: P110.
units.anchor: The following statements are provided as examples for teachers

units.why: States "Clear and concise course policies and explicit instructions ... are key to compliance", urging instructors to be explicit about AI in policies and assignments: P09.
units.anchor: Clear and concise course policies and explicit instructions for course assignments and assessments related to

units.why: Sample statement: misconduct occurs "wherever AI assistance has been used when unauthorized, or when authorized, has not been disclosed". Classifies misuse as misconduct, P36; it also makes nondisclosure a violation.
units.anchor: Academic misconduct is present in an academic work wherever AI assistance has been used when
units.fit_note: Also makes failure to disclose authorized AI use a violation (P28).

units.why: Sample statement "Expect changes": rules "may need to change on short notice" - policy is provisional, P54.
units.anchor: the rules that are expressed in this syllabus may need to change on short notice

units.why: Allow-with-attribution sample: "you may submit material that contains AI-generated content" if documented, listing drafting outlines and sections. A permissive default for writing, P02; prose-specific.
units.anchor: you may submit material that contains AI-generated content, or is based on or derived from
units.fit_note: Applies to writing and requires documentation.

units.why: "Your documentation must make the process transparent" requires students to document AI use with the submission: P24.
units.anchor: Your documentation must make the process transparent

units.why: Open book sample: "The use of AI tools is permitted, provided you follow our standards for attribution". Allows AI on an exam with attribution; P02 chosen over P22 since it permits.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools is permitted, provided you follow our standards for attribution, validation,
units.fit_note: Applies to an open-book exam or quiz only.

units.why: Encourage sample: "We encourage the use of such AI resources to inform yourself about the field ... and to help your learning." Welcomes AI, P02.
units.anchor: We encourage the use of such AI resources to inform yourself about the field

units.why: "AI generated submissions cannot achieve a passing grade" sets a grading rule redesigned around AI: P35.
units.anchor: AI generated submissions cannot achieve a passing grade

units.why: The stated reason is "to ensure you are competent to surpass generative AI in the future"; skill-building rationale, nearest P41.
units.anchor: This is necessary to ensure you are competent to surpass generative AI in the future
units.fit_note: Frames the goal as being able to outperform AI, including in the workplace, not only practice builds skill.

units.why: The course "will produce, analyze, and provide AI-generated sample solutions. Your task will be to surpass them" - a baseline built from AI, P35.
units.anchor: we will produce, analyze, and provide AI-generated sample solutions

units.why: "You are taking full responsibility for AI-generated materials as if you had produced them yourself": students own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: You are taking full responsibility for AI-generated materials as if you had produced them yourself

units.why: "facts must be true" requires students to check AI output for accuracy; P31.
units.anchor: facts must be true
units.policy: Facts in AI-generated material must be true.
units.fit_note: Short statement; does not say AI is often wrong.

units.why: "A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use" requires keeping and submitting documentation of AI use and grades it: P26.
units.anchor: A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use throughout the
units.fit_note: Documentation is graded, which P26 does not mention.

units.why: Prohibit sample: "The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited in this course." Default ban, P01.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited in this course

units.why: "Closed Book Exam/Quiz The use of AI tools is not permitted." No AI on exams: P22.
units.anchor: Closed Book Exam/Quiz The use of AI tools is not permitted

units.why: Writing sample: "The use of generative AI tools is not permitted on writing assignments". A prose-specific ban, P18.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted on writing assignments in this course

units.why: Code sample: "The use of generative AI tools to develop code is strictly prohibited"; students may not have AI produce submitted code, P19.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools to develop code is strictly prohibited in this course

units.why: Attestation text "you attest that you are the only and original author of the code submitted" makes students own the submission, P29.
units.anchor: you attest that you are the only and original author of the code submitted

units.why: "These are only examples ... and should be amended to reflect UNT and departmental policies as well as specifics of the classroom": instructors adapt the rule, P04.
units.anchor: should be amended to reflect UNT and departmental policies as well as specifics of the
units.fit_note: Says samples must fit university and department policy and the classroom.

units.why: The guide links "Teaching Methods and Classroom Integration" articles, pointing instructors to further guidance: P115.
units.anchor: Teaching Methods and Classroom Integration

documents.unit: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
documents.title: Academic Integrity (CSE)
documents.stance_why: The AI section says "Unless a professor or instructor gives explicit 'authorization,' AI cannot be used to assist in the completion of assignments", so AI is banned unless permitted.
documents.summary: CSE department page on academic integrity and professionalism. A short AI section makes unauthorized AI use a cheating violation and tells students to ask instructors; the rest lists penalties and conduct rules.

units.why: "the 'unauthorized' use of any person or technology that assists in a student's assignment ... is considered cheating"; classifies unauthorized AI as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: is considered cheating under the UNT Student Academic Integrity Policy

units.why: "Unless a professor or instructor gives explicit 'authorization,' AI cannot be used" is a fallback ban when no permission exists: P06.
units.anchor: Unless a professor or instructor gives explicit "authorization," AI cannot be used

units.why: "Doing so will result in a 'cheating' violation" states the consequence of unauthorized AI use; the classification is P36, with no specific penalty.
units.anchor: Doing so will result in a "cheating" violation

units.why: "if uncertain contact the instructor prior to using AI tools" is the ask-first rule: P10.
units.anchor: if uncertain contact the instructor prior to using AI tools

units.why: "A more complete procedures and guidelines will be made available soon" admits the AI section is provisional: P54.
units.anchor: A more complete procedures and guidelines will be made available soon

units.why: Lists consequences of integrity violations, including "Removal from the student's degree program" and loss of TA/IA/RA positions. Stated penalties apply to the AI "cheating" violation, P37; not AI-specific.
units.anchor: Removal from the student's degree program
units.fit_note: General integrity consequences, not written for AI specifically.

units.why: "Two reported and verified academic integrity violations in two separate courses with two separate instructors" lead to removal from CSE programs: an escalating penalty, P37.
units.anchor: Two reported and verified academic integrity violations in two separate courses with two separate instructors
units.fit_note: General integrity penalty; AI is a cheating violation under this page.

units.why: TAs or IAs who facilitate violations face "Immediate expulsion"; this binds staff and sets a penalty, P37.
units.anchor: Immediate expulsion – verified assisting other students in cheating
units.fit_note: Binds TAs and IAs and is not AI-specific.

units.why: "Examinations are to involve no talking, no sharing/discussing, notes, or internet use unless authorized", with an automatic F. Closed-resource exam rule, nearest P22; AI is not named.
units.anchor: Examinations are to involve no talking, no sharing/discussing, notes, or internet use unless authorized
units.fit_note: AI is not mentioned; rule is no internet or notes on exams.

units.why: "Violations will result in an automatic F in the course" is a concrete penalty stated in advance for exam cheating: P37.
units.anchor: Violations will result in an automatic F in the course

units.why: "It is the student's responsibility to be aware of these policies. Lack of awareness is not grounds for appeal": students must know the rules, P78.
units.anchor: It is the student's responsibility to be aware of these policies

units.why: The department says its actions are "corrective, educationally sound, fundamentally fair, and based on reliable evidence", an educative response stance with an evidence note; P68.
units.anchor: the Department's actions are intended to be corrective, educationally sound, fundamentally fair, and based on
units.fit_note: Also says actions rest on reliable evidence (P69); not AI-specific.

units.why: "If you are reported for academic integrity violations, the academic integrity appeals process is available" gives accused students a way to respond: P64.
units.anchor: If you are reported for academic integrity violations, the academic integrity appeals process is available

units.why: "It is critical to reach out to instructors ... to clarify what constitutes an academic integrity violation when uncertain" is an ask-when-unsure rule: P10.
units.anchor: It is critical to reach out to instructors, or relevant faculty and staff, to clarify
units.fit_note: General integrity, not AI-specific.

units.why: Advises syllabi to include "All department policies on Academic Integrity and Student Conduct apply for this course", asking instructors to point to the department policy: P09.
units.anchor: All department policies on Academic Integrity and Student Conduct apply for this course
units.fit_note: Suggested wording refers to department policy rather than stating AI rules.

units.why: "Note all deviations from the department guidelines in the syllabus explicitly" lets instructors differ from the department default if stated; nearest P04.
units.anchor: Note all deviations from the department guidelines in the syllabus explicitly
units.fit_note: Instructor exceptions are allowed but must be written out in the syllabus.

notes: Computing layer page is general integrity; units from penalty and conduct sections are flagged with fit_note because AI is not named. No school layer found; course layer deferred. Topic codes are free-form since AGENT_BRIEF.md was not found.
